messages:
sara_sales: Hey team — enterprise POC asked for our incident response & breach notification timeline for contract review. They specifically asked: if customer data is affected, how quickly do we notify customers and regulators? They also asked if we can commit to a 72-hour regulator notification SLA. Need a succinct customer-facing line + a slightly longer security-bizops answer for the SIG/CAIQ reviewer.

max_security: Short version for sales: we notify affected customers promptly upon confirmation of a material impact; regulator notifications are handled in accordance with applicable law and the contract. For presales, avoid a flat 72-hour regulator SLA. Offer: we can commit to reasonable efforts to notify affected customers within 48 hours of confirmation and work with customers on regulator steps as required. Link to internal IR doc: https://redwood.example/internal/security/incident-response

olivia_se: Can you give a 1-line for the deck and a 4‑bullet explainer we can paste into the SIG/CAIQ free text answers? POC needs a sample timeline + RACI (who owns comms, who provides logs).

tim_sre: POC-friendly timeline (short): detect -> confirm -> contain -> notify -> remediations/report. Typical timings we share in a POC: detect (minutes to hours depending on telemetry), confirm (up to 24 hours while we triage), initial customer notification (within 48 hours of confirmation), detailed incident report (7–30 days depending on scope). RACI: Redwood sec ops detects/confirms, SRE contains/mitigates, Customer success + Sales lead customer comms, Security provides full report. Include rollback/canary notes when relevant.

max_security: SIG/CAIQ mapping notes you can drop into the questionnaire: we map IR controls (IR-1..IR-8) to our policies and artifacts: incident response plan, tabletop runbooks, forensics logs, communication templates, and post-incident remediation reports. Sample free-text: "Redwood maintains a documented incident response program; we notify affected customers promptly upon confirmation and comply with regulatory obligations as required by law and contract. Artifacts available on request: incident playbooks, timelines, and post-incident reports." Also call out data categories: affected customer data = customer identifiers, prompt/response payloads, embeddings, telemetry/logs (we do not store plaintext customer secrets unless explicitly configured).

sara_sales: Customer asked point blank: "Will you sign 72-hour notification?" — what's our negotiation stance so I can reply without legal loop forever?

max_security: Negotiation stance: default public docs/sales language = notify affected customers promptly (we recommend saying "within 48 hours of confirmation"). For enterprise deals we can consider contractual language like "commercially reasonable efforts to notify affected customers within 72 hours of confirmation" but regulator notification commitments are legal territory and may vary by jurisdiction — route to Legal for any fixed regulator SLA. If they push hard, offer an Enterprise Security Addendum with response time commitments + quarterly runbooks.

olivia_se: For the POC checklist: can we include a minimum access list + logs we need and a sample notification template? Customer wants to see we have playbooks.

tim_sre: POC checklist snippet (paste into POC doc):
```
- Point of contact for customer (name, phone, email)
- Access to delivery logs and request traces for the test tenant (read-only)
- SIEM/alerting export access (if available) or scheduled log dump cadence
- Agreed timezone window for high-signal testing
- Communication channel for incident updates (email + slack channel)
```
Sample initial notification template (short): "We have confirmed an incident affecting [scope]. Redwood Security is investigating; we will provide an initial impact assessment within 48 hours and a follow-up report within X days. For immediate concerns contact [POC]."

incident-bot: Reminder: use IR template IR-TPL-1 when compiling POC artifacts. Attach exec summary + timeline + sanitized logs.

max_security: Also flag for sales: if the customer requests SIG-proofs (raw artifacts), we typically provide redacted artifacts and a SOC/attestation or MSA-provided audit channels. Full raw forensics requires an NDA/scoped forensics engagement.

sara_sales: Perfect — I'll update the POC brief with the 48h customer-notify line + the checklist and attach the SIG mapping. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
